references.text: The burnt offering was to be slaughtered at the entrance of the tent of meeting, before the Lord, in the same place where the sin offering was to be slaughtered.
Describes that the sin offering is to be slaughtered in the same place as the burnt offering, before the Lord.
The sin offering for a common Israelite was also to be slaughtered at the place of the burnt offering.
Repeats the instruction that the sin offering must be slaughtered where the burnt offering is slaughtered.
The grain offering is described as most holy (קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים), the same designation used for the sin offering here.
The grain offering is also called most holy, in the same way as the sin offering.
The guilt offering is also described as most holy (קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים).
The guilt offering is most holy and must be eaten in a holy place, like the sin offering.
Moses confirms that the sin offering is most holy and given to the priests.
The altar is described as most holy; the same terminology is used for the sin offering.
Ezekiel describes the most holy offerings, including the sin offering, which are to be eaten in a holy place.
The priests shall eat the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering in the future temple.
